subject: LedgerWorks — post-call econ decision brief & pilot asks
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie@ledgerworks.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: LedgerWorks — post-call econ decision brief & pilot asks

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the time today. Short recap of the call, the cost levers we discussed, and suggested next steps so your team can share with procurement/finance. I’ve attached a one-page pilot scope and the demo recording for reference.

Top-line: primary constraint is monthly budget (~$85k cap for pilot) and a hard requirement to see predictable unit economics before a 2027 expansion. You called out two main goals: 1) reduce per-user inference cost for conversational flows used by support agents, and 2) preserve latency under 300ms P95 for agent-facing queries.

Key pain points (as we heard)
- High token bills when agents use long context/history and multi-turn retrieval.
- Unpredictable bursts during peak times that spike north of budget.
- Limited internal infra ops for model tuning — you want a partner that can operationalize levers, not just hand off a model.

Assumptions we used on the call (please correct if off):
- Current monthly tokens for the targeted workflow: ~120M tokens/month (inference only).
- Average prompt+response length: 420 tokens.
- Current cost baseline (your estimate): ~$0.0006/token (third-party provider blended rate).

Recommended cost/TCO levers we propose for the pilot
1) Batching + dynamic micro-batching: reduces per-token GPU overhead for high-concurrency bursts. Expected saving: 15–25% on token compute for this workload shape.
2) Prefix/KV caching for agent context: cache last 4 turns per user to avoid reprocessing repeated history — expect 20–30% token reduction on reads when cache hit rate > 40%.
3) Model variant & quantization mix: use a 7B quantized variant for routine lookups and a 13B non-quant for escalations; this hybrid routing lowers average cost ~10–18% while preserving quality.
4) Autoscaling + reserved burst pools: cap predictable baseline on Reserved Dedicated capacity and allow short burst using on-demand hosts to avoid overprovisioning.

Preliminary TCO illustration (pilot month) — conservative estimate
- Baseline (no changes): 120M tokens * $0.0006 = $72,000
- Combined levers (batching + cache + hybrid routing): estimated reduction 38% -> adjusted spend ~$44,640
- Redwood pilot fee + monitoring + support (monthly): $18,000
- Estimated total month 1: $62,640 (net reduction vs baseline ~13%)

Why this matters (ROI framing)
- If we validate cache hit rates and batching behavior in a 6-week pilot, projected steady-state annualized savings for the target workflow are ~$170k to $220k vs current run-rate, without degrading latency targets.

Proposed pilot scope & asks (attached)
- 6-week pilot focused on the support-agent flow for a subset of 1,200 agents (staged roll).
- Integration: token-level telemetry + sample prompt set provided by LedgerWorks (we’ll sign NDAs).
- Success criteria: 30%+ reduction in inference spend for the flow OR latency P95 < 300ms + similar/better CSAT on agent responses.
- Pricing ask: pilot monthly cap at $85k with a proposed Redwood contribution/discount schedule we can finalize after you confirm procurement constraints.

Next steps
1) Sophie: confirm pilot budget cap and any procurement timing windows this month.
2) LedgerWorks security/compliance contact: share SOC2/AWSP evidence point-of-contact for a short checklist.
3) Redwood: deliver a 6-week pilot SOW & a 3-month simulated TCO spreadsheet by EOD Thu (attached).

Attachments: pilot-scope.xlsx (pilot scope & pricing bands), demo-recording.mp4 (call demo)

Thanks — happy to hop back on with finance/procurement if helpful.

— Camila

From: Sophie Turner <sophie@ledgerworks.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: LedgerWorks Procurement <procurement@ledgerworks.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: LedgerWorks — post-call econ decision brief & pilot asks

Camila — thanks for the clear summary. This aligns closely with what we heard internally. A few clarifications and requests from our side: 

1) Budget & timeline: $85k/month is the current upper bound for a pilot our finance sponsor will approve. We can do 6 weeks if you can pro-rate month 1. Procurement wants to see a realistic month-1 cap and a capped overage policy.

2) Security: we need the SOC2 type II report and a quick checklist of where logs are stored (retention) and who has access to token data. Can you route that to our security contact (cc’d).

3) Metrics & telemetry: we’ll provide sample prompt sets and a small labeled eval set for quality checks. We also need a standard template for how you’ll report token reductions week-over-week.

4) Procurement ask: we prefer a 30% refundable credit toward first paid month if pilot demonstrates >30% cost reduction. Is that something Redwood can consider?

If you send the SOW and the 1-page security evidence by EOD Thu we’ll start the procurement review.

— Sophie
Sophie Turner | Head of Digital Ops | LedgerWorks

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LedgerWorks — post-call econ decision brief & pilot asks

Quick internal note — Sophie’s ask for a 30% refundable credit is notable. Suggest we propose two options back:

A) Standard pilot: monthly cap $85k, 15% Redwood pilot discount on service fees, pilot refundable credit of 15% applied to first paid month if success criteria met.
B) Accelerated: monthly cap $85k, 25% Redwood contribution (discount + credit) but requires sign-off from Sales Director (Marissa) and approval of a limited 90-day Dedicated burst allocation (we can commit to reserved baseline sizing).

Operational asks we’ll need from Marissa: 1) approve up-to-$XXk pilot contribution authority or confirm escalation path; 2) confirm we can allocate burst reserved capacity for LW pilot (we’ll pencil in 2 gpus reserved for baseline + ability to burst).

I can draft the SOW text for both options; Camila will send to Sophie.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Sophie — appreciate the quick turnaround. We can do the following and will attach a clean SOW + a short security evidence sheet in this email thread (see Drive link in related links).

Confirmed items
- Pilot structure: 6-week pilot, pro-rated month-1 cap to keep spend <= $85k.
- Overage policy: any overage requires explicit written approval; we’ll provide daily spend dashboards and a hard alert at 85% of the cap.
- Discounts/credits: propose Option A as Marcus outlined (15% pilot discount + refundable 15% credit to first paid month on success). Option B available if Marissa signs off — I’ll escalate if you prefer that route.

What we’ll send by EOD Thu
- Final SOW with Option A & Option B pricing bands.
- SOC2 evidence sheet + retention/ACL summary for token telemetry.
- Week-by-week metrics template we’ll use for the pilot (token count, cache hit rate, average batch size, latency P95).

Please confirm procurement contact and the best day/time next week for a short kickoff (30m) so we can align the sample prompt set ingestion and telemetry keys. Once procurement confirms, we’ll issue a DocuSign SOW link and kick off engineering onboarding.

Thanks — Camila
